rows.title: Policy
rows.figure: Fed Oct 28 hold ~90%, Dec hike ~73–82%; BoC Oct 28 hike ~75–80%; RBNZ tonight 8:00 PM CT hike ~85–90%; ECB Oct 29 hold ~95%; BoJ Oct 30 hold ~98%; RBA Nov 3 ~50%; BoE Nov 5 hike ~90–97%
rows.read: Five central banks decide in the next four days, and most still lean toward raising rates because energy keeps inflation high. Strong US figures today made a December Fed hike look more likely, which helped the dollar. New Zealand goes first tonight, with Canada and the Fed on Wednesday.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: US consumer confidence Oct 91.7 (fc 81.2); durable goods Sep +1.8% (fc +0.6%); new home sales Sep 676K (fc 660K); French consumer confidence Oct 80 (lowest since 2013)
rows.read: The US economy keeps beating expectations: households are more upbeat and business orders are rising. In France, consumer mood sank to a 13-year low. That gap between a strong US and a soft euro area favours the dollar over the euro.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: UK BRC shop prices Oct +2.1% y/y (fc 1.6%); BoJ trend inflation Sep 3.2%; US 1-yr price expectations ~5.8% (Conference Board); Australia Q3 CPI tonight 7:30 PM CT (trimmed ~+1.0% q/q fc)
rows.read: Energy is still pushing inflation above target in most big economies, and it is spreading into shop prices in Britain and into underlying prices in Japan. American households still expect prices to rise quickly. That keeps central banks leaning toward hikes; Australia's inflation figures tonight are the next big reading.

rows.title: Risk
rows.figure: S&P 500 and Nasdaq higher (Nasdaq ~+1% mid-afternoon); USD/JPY 157.80 (+0.19%); USD/CHF 0.8289 (+0.17%); gold ~$4,018; Brent −0.9%
rows.read: Markets were calm: US stocks rose, led by big tech, and oil eased as talks with Iran went on. That cut demand for safe havens, so the yen and franc slipped. A failed round of talks or a confirmed hit on Saudi oil would quickly reverse that.

rows.title: Terms of trade
rows.figure: Brent $114.80 (−0.9%); WTI $99.77 (−2.0%); Houthi claim on Ras Tanura unconfirmed; UBS year-end Brent ~$110
rows.read: Oil slipped as talks with Iran continued, though attacks in the Gulf keep most of the war premium in the price. Cheaper oil is a small relief for energy importers like Japan and the euro area and a small loss for Canada.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: CFTC Oct 20: funds strongly against CAD (sharply added), against NZD (sharply added) and EUR (added), for GBP (real money strongly against), for AUD (real money strongly against), leaning against JPY (flipped), strongly for gold (trimmed)
rows.read: Hedge funds are betting most heavily against the Canadian dollar and the kiwi, even though both central banks are expected to hike this week, so those bets are exposed if the hikes come with signals of more. In the pound and the Aussie, hedge funds and long-term investors take opposite sides.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: UK Budget Wed Oct 28 ~7:30 AM CT; French revenue-section vote moved to Nov 3; France–Germany 10-year gap ~167 bp; Moody's France Aa3, negative outlook
rows.read: Britain's first Budget from Chancellor John Healey lands on Wednesday morning, and heavier borrowing could unsettle UK bonds and the pound. In France, the budget vote slipped again and consumer gloom deepened, which keeps a weight on the euro.
